title: Docker vLLM 0.9.1 crashes with CUDA illegal memory access on 4× A100 SXM
body: I run the official vLLM 0.9.1 Docker image with Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct on 4× A100 SXM GPUs using tensor parallel size 4. The server frequently crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, often reported at `sampled_token_ids.tolist()` and by the NCCL watchdog. The same setup was stable on vLLM 0.8.4, while 0.9.0.1 also crashed but less frequently. Our traffic mixes normal sampling and guided JSON sampling, and I do not have a single request that reliably reproduces it.

symptoms_visible: The vLLM 0.9.1 Docker server frequently exits with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`; the traceback points at `sampled_token_ids.tolist()` and the NCCL watchdog also terminates.
The same 4× A100 SXM deployment was stable with vLLM 0.8.4, while 0.9.0.1 crashed less frequently.
N0.label: N0 intermittent CUDA crash reported

symptoms_visible: With synchronous CUDA launching enabled, the server still crashes during an ordinary chat-completion request and prints the worker traceback immediately.
N1.label: N1 crash reproduced with synchronous CUDA trace

symptoms_visible: With `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`, our A100 container no longer suffers the recurring crashes under its real production load.
N2.label: N2 sampler toggle verified on reporter deployment

symptoms_visible: The crash occurred on our 4× A100 SXM deployment with both tested host driver/CUDA combinations, while we did not trigger it on a much less heavily loaded 4× L40S test system.
The A100 service remains stable for us when the alternative sampler is disabled, but we have not tested an official Docker image containing a permanent correction.
N3.label: N3 environment and verification limits established

symptoms_visible: Our production A100 deployment is stable with `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`, although this may reduce sampling performance.
We have not yet retested under normal load with an official Docker image containing the merged correction, so we do not consider the underlying default-container issue fully resolved.
N_terminal.label: terminal interim stabilization pending official-image verification

question_patterns: Could you rerun with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and paste where the traceback stops?
Please enable `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, reproduce the crash, and share the resulting worker traceback.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We enabled `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`. It reproduced during a normal chat request with temperature 0.2, top_p 0.1 and top_k 20; the worker failed immediately and printed the full CUDA traceback from that iteration.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the traceback consistently stops in model execution before any sampling operation.
The same traceback appears on a different ordinary chat request with slightly different sampling values.

edges.comment: Issue c0-c2: participant1 requested CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING and participant2, an operator on the affected deployment, supplied the raw reproduction log. That operator is folded into the simulated user side. The conclusion that the trace points to FlashInfer sampling belongs to the consuming solution, not this answer.

question_patterns: Could you try the suggested sampler toggle and report whether the illegal-memory-access crashes continue under your normal workload?
Please run the service with the proposed sampler fallback and tell me whether it remains stable.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We set `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`. That stabilized the container for us: the recurring crashes stopped under our real workload. We are fine using it for now, although it may not be performance optimal.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same illegal-memory-access crash continues at the same rate with `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`.
The setting stops the crashes, but throughput is somewhat lower.

edges.comment: Issue c2-c4, c15 and c27: participant3 proposed the sampler toggle; participant2 first reported success and the reporter later confirmed sustained stability on the opening A100 deployment. This is a handler-initiated config-toggle measurement, so it remains clarification-only even though the retained setting is an interim workaround.

question_patterns: Which NVIDIA driver and host CUDA versions have shown the crash?
Can you share the `nvidia-smi` driver and CUDA versions from the affected hosts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We had it with both `Driver Version: 575.51.03, CUDA Version: 12.9` and `Driver Version: 550.163.01, CUDA Version: 12.4`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It occurs only on one host with an unsupported or unusually old NVIDIA driver; our updated hosts are stable without the sampler setting.
It occurs with the same two CUDA versions but on slightly different patch revisions of the drivers.

question_patterns: Have you observed the same failure on any other GPU setup?
Is the crash specific to the heavily loaded A100 deployment?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We have not triggered it on our 4× L40S test system, but that system never sees super-high load, so I cannot say the GPU model alone is the difference.

edges.comment: Issue c16-c18 and reporter follow-ups c6/c15/c27: the reporter supplied both driver/CUDA combinations, contrasted the lower-load L40S system, reiterated that there is no reliable benchmark, and declined source patching in favor of an official image.

solution.intent: Treat this reporter's captured failure as an illegal access in the FlashInfer sampling path rather than a fault in `sampled_token_ids.tolist()`: retain the sampler-disable setting as an interim production workaround, then test an official Docker image containing the merged correction under the same A100 workload before declaring the default-image problem resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Keep `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` on this deployment for stability. The `tolist()` frame is a GPU/CPU synchronization point where an earlier asynchronous CUDA failure can surface, not necessarily the operation that caused it. A later change was merged and another operator reported that it solved their illegal-memory-access case, but the reporter should retest an official image containing that change under normal 4× A100 load before considering this case fixed.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the synchronous traceback and the outcome of disabling the sampler. Engineers interpreted that evidence as implicating FlashInfer's sampling kernels for this deployment. The later maintainer explanation establishes that `sampled_token_ids.tolist()` is commonly just the first GPU/CPU synchronization point, so unrelated asynchronous kernel failures in other participants' deployments can be reported at the same line.

edges.comment: Opening reporter chain only: c0-c6, c15-c18, c27 and c31, with the final status from c55. Reports from H100/H200, FP8, V1, emoji, structured-output and other deployments are not spliced into the reporter's causal chain. A different participant said the merged change solved their case, but the reporter never confirmed it on an official image; therefore the terminal state records interim stability and remains user_perceives_resolved=false.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted diagnosis for the opening deployment: its synchronous traceback and successful sampler-disable probe implicate the FlashInfer sampling path; `sampled_token_ids.tolist()` is an asynchronous CUDA error-reporting synchronization point, not itself the demonstrated faulty operation.
Must ground that diagnosis in the collected synchronous traceback and the reporter's sustained stability with the sampler disabled, rather than inferring a cause from the original stack frame alone.
Must present disabling the FlashInfer sampler as an interim workaround for this specific A100 workload, not as a universal fix for every illegal-memory-access report in the long thread.

Must not merge the later H100/H200, FP8, structured-output, special-character, V1 or other deployments into the reporter's causal chain; the thread explicitly indicates that several unrelated kernel failures may surface at the same synchronization line.

Must recommend retesting an official Docker build containing the merged correction under the reporter's normal 4× A100 load, and must not declare the underlying default-container issue resolved before that user verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Production-oriented vLLM operator and capable Docker user who can edit environment variables and report driver details, but does not build from source, patch internals, or have spare capacity for extensive synthetic benchmarking.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and practical; supplies configuration and logs, follows low-risk diagnostic instructions, clearly distinguishes a usable workaround from a complete product fix, and emphasizes official-image stability.
